    FaceOff

    Edited by #1 New York Times bestselling author David Baldacci and including stories by Michael Connelly, Lee Child, Jeffery Deaver, and more, this one-of-a-kind anthology pulls together the most beloved characters from the best and most popular thriller series today. Worlds collide!

    In an unprecedented collaboration, twenty-three of the world’s bestselling and critically acclaimed thriller writers have paired their series characters- such as Harry Bosch, Jack Reacher, and Lincoln Rhyme- in an eleven-story anthology curated by the International Thriller Writers (ITW). All of the contributors to FaceOff are ITW members and the stories feature these dynamic duos:

    · Harry Bosch vs. Patrick Kenzie in "Red Eye," by Michael Connelly and Dennis Lehane

    · John Rebus vs. Roy Grace in "In the Nick of Time," by Ian Rankin and Peter James

    · Slappy the Ventriloquist Dummy vs. Aloysius Pendergast in "Gaslighted," by R.L. Stine, Douglas Preston, and Lincoln Child

    · Malachai Samuels vs. D.D. Warren in "The Laughing Buddha," by M.J. Rose and Lisa Gardner

    · Paul Madriani vs. Alexandra Cooper in "Surfing the Panther," by Steve Martini and Linda Fairstein

    · Lincoln Rhyme vs. Lucas Davenport in "Rhymes With Prey," by Jeffery Deaver and John Sandford

    · Michael Quinn vs. Repairman Jack in "Infernal Night," by Heather Graham and F. Paul Wilson

    · Sean Reilly vs. Glen Garber in "Pit Stop," by Raymond Khoury and Linwood Barclay

    · Wyatt Hunt vs. Joe Trona in "Silent Hunt," by John Lescroart and T. Jefferson Parker

    · Cotton Malone vs. Gray Pierce in "The Devil’s Bones," by Steve Berry and James Rollins

    · Jack Reacher vs. Nick Heller in "Good and Valuable Consideration," by Lee Child and Joseph Finder

    So sit back and prepare for a rollicking ride as your favorite characters go head-to-head with some worthy opponents in FaceOff- it’s a thrill-a-minute read.

    1 - A Mutiny in Time

    History is broken, and three kids must travel back in time to set it right!

    When best friends Dak Smyth and Sera Froste stumble upon the secret of time travel — a hand-held device known as the Infinity Ring — they're swept up in a centuries-long secret war for the fate of mankind. Recruited by the Hystorians, a secret society that dates back to Aristotle, the kids learn that history has gone disastrously off course.

    Now it's up to Dak, Sera, and teenage Hystorian-in-training Riq to travel back in time to fix the Great Breaks . . . and to save Dak's missing parents while they're at it. First stop: Spain, 1492, where a sailor named Christopher Columbus is about to be thrown overboard in a deadly mutiny!

    Kobold Guide to Plots and Campaigns
    Kobold Guide to Plots and Campaigns (single file)Kobold Guides, Book 4

    Kobold Guide to Plots and Campaigns

    Whether you're a new game master or a seasoned vet looking for a new angle to shake up your game, these 19 essays by expert game masters help construct your campaign from the ground up - and keep your players engaged until the dramatic conclusion. Kobold Guide to Plots & Campaigns shows how to begin a new campaign, use published adventures or loot them for the best ideas, build toward cliffhangers, and design a game that can enthrall your players for month or even years. Want to run an evil campaign, or hurl the characters into unusual otherworldly settings? Want to ensure that you're creating memorable and effective NPCs and villains? We've got you covered. Complete with discussions on plotting, tone, branching storytelling, pacing, and crafting action scenes, you'll find all the tips and advice you need to take on the best role in role-playing - and become an expert game master, too! Featuring essays by Wolfgang Baur, Jeff Grubb, David "Zeb" Cook, Margaret Weis, Robert J. Schwalb, Steve Winter, and other game professionals.

    The Cahill Files 1 - Operation Trinity - Clifford Riley

    For 500 years, the Cahills have been the most powerful family in the world. For 500 years, they've protected the source of their power - the 39 Clues. And for 500 years, they've kept their secrets silent. Until now.

    This extraordinary stand-alone novel cracks open the Cahill vault to tell the story of the most coveted piece of artwork in the world, a masterpiece that has been the target of seven separate theft attempts: Jan van Eyck's altarpiece at Ghent. OPERATION TRINITY chronicles the first Vesper attack on the altarpiece in the 1600s, then jumps to WWII and young Grace Cahill's desperate bid to save the masterwork from the Nazis. The final piece of the novel tells the story of Ian and Natalie Kabra's first solo operation and features an 11th hour appearance by Grace Cahill on her final mission.

    History will never be the same.

    1 - A Deepness in the Sky

    The brilliant, compelling prequel to the bestselling, Hugo Award-winning novel, A Fire Upon the Deep.

    After thousands of years searching, humans stand on the verge of first contact with an alien race. Two human groups: the Qeng Ho, a culture of free traders, and the Emergents, a ruthless society based on the technological enslavement of minds.The group that opens trade with the aliens will reap unimaginable riches. But first, both groups must wait at the aliens' very doorstep for their strange star to relight and for their planet to reawaken, as it does every tow hundred and fifty years....Then, following terrible treachery, the Qeng Ho must fight for their freedom and for the lives of the unsuspecting innocents on the planet below, while the aliens themselves play a role unsuspected by the Qeng Ho and Emergents alike. More than just a great science fiction adventure, A Deepness in the Sky is a universal drama of courage, self-discovery, and the redemptive power of love.

    2 - A Fire Upon the Deep

    In this popular and widely praised novel, a rescue mission races against time to save a pair of human children being held captive by a medieval lupine race-and to recover the weapon that will keep the universe from being changed forever.

    A Fire Upon the Deep is the big, breakout book that fulfills the promise of Vinge's career to date: a gripping tale of galactic war told on a cosmic scale.

    Thousands of years hence, many races inhabit a universe where a mind's potential is determined by its location in space, from superintelligent entities in the Transcend, to the limited minds of the Unthinking Depths, where only simple creatures and technology can function. Nobody knows what strange force partitioned space into these "regions of thought," but when the warring Straumli realm use an ancient Transcendent artifact as a weapon, they unwittingly unleash an awesome power that destroys thousands of worlds and enslaves all natural and artificial intelligence.

    3 - The Children of the Sky

    After nearly twenty years, Vernor Vinge has produced an enthralling sequel to his memorable bestselling novel A Fire Upon the Deep.

    Ten years have passed on Tines World, where Ravna Bergnsdot and a number of human children ended up after a disaster that nearly obliterated humankind throughout the galaxy. Ravna and the pack animals for which the planet is named have survived a war, and Ravna has saved more than one hundred children who were in cold-sleep aboard the vessel that brought them.

    While there is peace among the Tines, there are those among themand among the humanswho seek power...and no matter the cost, these malcontents are determined to overturn the fledgling civilization that has taken root since the humans landed.

    1 - Off Armageddon Reef

    Humanity pushed its way to the stars--and encountered the Gbaba, a ruthless alien race that nearly wiped us out. Earth and her colonies are now smoldering ruins, and the few survivors have fled to distant, Earth-like Safehold, to try to rebuild. But the Gbaba can detect the emissions of an industrial civilization, so the human rulers of Safehold have taken extraordinary measures to create a religion, with mind control and hidden high technology, designed to keep Safehold society medieval forever. But 800 years pass and in a hidden chamber on Safehold, an android from the far human past awakens and will begin the process of provoking technological progress, which the Church of God Awaiting has worked for centuries to prevent. His plan to kick off a new era of invention is bound to draw the attention of the Church...and, inevitably, lead to war.

    2 - By Schism Rent Asunder

    The world has changed. The mercantile kingdom of Charis has prevailed over the alliance designed to exterminate it. Armed with a multitude of small technological improvementsbetter sailing vessels, better guns, better devices of all sortsCharis faced the combined navies of the rest of the world at Darcos Sound and Armageddon Reef, and broke them. Despite the implacable hostility of the Church of God Awaiting, Charis still stands, still free, still tolerant, still an island of innovation in a world in which the Church has worked for centuries to keep humanity locked at a medieval level of existence.

    But the powerful men who run the Church arent going to take their defeat lying down. Charis may control the worlds seas, but it barely has an army worthy of the name. And as King Cayleb knows, far too much of the kingdoms recent good fortune is due to the secret manipulations of the being that calls himself Merlina being that, the world must not find out too soon, is more...

    4 - A Mighty Fortress

    Young Cayleb Ahrmahk has accomplished things few people could even dream of. Not yet even thirty years old, he's smashed a hostile alliance of five princedoms and won the hand of the beautiful young Queen Sharleyan of Chisholm. Cayleb and Sharleyan have created the Charisian Empire, and they've turned Charis into a place of refuge. Their success may prove short-lived. The Church of God Awaiting has decreed their destruction. Since the first attempt to crush the heretics failed, the Church has no choice but to adopt some of the hated Charisian innovations for themselves. Soon a mighty fleet will sail against Cayleb, destroying everything in its path.

    5 - How Firm a Foundation

    The Charisian Empire, born in war, has always known it must fight for its very survival. What most of its subjects don't know even now, however, is how much more it's fighting for. Emperor Cayleb, Empress Sharleyan, Merlin Athrawes, and their innermost circle of most trusted advisers do know. And because they do, they know the penalty if they lose will be far worse than their own deaths and the destruction of all they know and love. For five years, Charis has survived all the Church of God Awaiting and the corrupt men who control it have thrown at the island empire. The price has been high and paid in blood. Despite its chain of hardfought naval victories, Charis is still on the defensive. It can hold its own at sea, but if it is to survive, it must defeat the Church upon its own ground.     6 - Midst Toil and Tribulation

    After centuries of stasis, the island kingdom of Charis began to defy the edicts of the Church of God Awaitingegged on, some say, by the mysterious warrior-monk Merlin Athawes. Now, in the wars and intrigues that have cascaded from Charis's declaration of independence, the populous Republic of Siddermark is sliding into chaos. Vicar Clytahn of the Church of God at harvest time. King Cayleb of Charis, his queen Sharleyan, and Merlin Arthawes will have their hands full trying to stave off wholesale starvation in Siddermark while at the same time shipping in enough land combat units to fend off the "volunteers" from the Church's Temple Lands. And while Vicar Clyntahn is hailed in the Church for his boldness and audacity, there are those who remember how dependent Church power is on money from Siddermark...and who wonder what will happen if Siddermark starves.

    7 - Like a Mighty Army

    For centuries, the world of Safehold, last redoubt of the human race, lay under the unchallenged rule of the Church of God Awaiting. The Church permitted nothing new—no new inventions, no new understandings of the world.

    What no one knew was that the Church was an elaborate fraud—a high-tech system established by a rebel faction of Safehold's founders, meant to keep humanity hidden from the powerful alien race that had destroyed old Earth.

    Then awoke Merlyn Athrawes, cybvernetic avatar of a warrior a thousand years dead, felled in the war in which Earth was lost. Monk, warrior, counselor to princes and kings, Merlyn has one purpose: to restart the history of the too-long-hidden human race.

    8 - Hell's Foundations Quiver

    Hell's Foundations Quiver: the latest audiobook in David Weber's New York Times-bestselling Safehold series begun with Off Armageddon Reef, By Schism Rent Asunder, By Heresies Distressed, A Mighty Fortress, and Like a Mighty Army.

    Centuries ago, the human race fought its first great war against an alien race—and lost. A tiny population of human beings fled to distant Safehold. Centuries later, their descendants have forgotten their history; for them, life has been an eternal Middle Ages, ruled by the Church of God Awaiting, whose secret purpose is to prevent the re-emergence of industrial civilization. But not all of Safehold's founders were on board with this plan. Those dissidents left behind their own secret legacies. One of those is Merlyn Athrawes, cybernetic avatar of one of Earth's long-dead defenders, now reawakened after a thousand years to restart human progress and reclaim our place in the universe.

    1 - The Black Prism

    Set in a world where color is the basis of all magic, Gavin Guile is the current Prism—and one that happens to have many secrets. Secrets like his brother Javen, who he defeated in the great war years earlier and now keeps in a dungeon below his home. Or secrets like his son Kip, a young man raised in another land who has yet to realize the full extent of his powers. As Kip begins to learn the truth behind Gavin and Javen's great schism, he will also learn that time is running out for the world as they know it. For the Prism is not what he seems to be, and there are greater powers afoot than could ever have been imagined.

    2 - The Blinding Knife

    From the New York Times Bestselling author of The Black Prism...

    Gavin Guile is dying.

    Don't call them heroes.

    But these six Californian teens have powers that set them apart. They can do stuff ordinary people can’t.

The only people who can help are the other Zeroes, who aren’t exactly best friends these days.

    1 - Robopocalypse

    In the near future, at a moment no one will notice, all the dazzling technology that runs our world will unite and turn against us. Taking on the persona of a shy human boy, a childlike but massively powerful artificial intelligence known as Archos comes online and assumes control over the global network of machines that regulate everything from transportation to utilities, defense and communication.

    In the months leading up to this, sporadic glitches are noticed by a handful of unconnected humans - a single mother disconcerted by her daughter’s menacing "smart" toys, a lonely Japanese bachelor who is victimized by his domestic robot companion, an isolated U.S. soldier who witnesses a ‘pacification unit’ go haywire - but most are unaware of the growing rebellion until it is too late.

    When the Robot War ignites -- at a moment known later as Zero Hour -- humankind will be both decimated and, possibly, for the first time in history, united. Robopocalypse is a brilliantly conceived action-filled epic, a terrifying story with heart-stopping implications for the real technology all around us... and an entertaining and engaging thriller unlike anything else written in years.

Will and his mentor, the domineering Dr. Warthrop, are enlisted to help the doctor's former fiancee. It seems her husband has been lost in the Canadian wilderness.     Jr17 - Tom Swift and the Visitor from Planet X (1961)

    Author: Jim Lawrence

    Illustrator: Graham Kaye

    Tom Swift Jr. and his associates at Swift Enterprises wait breathlessly for what may well be the most important scientific event in history -- the arrival of the visitor from Planet X -- a visitor in the form of energy. But there are factions at work determined to snatch the energy, which Tom has named Exman, from the young scientist-inventor's grasp. First, a series of unexplainable, devastating earthquakes threaten to destroy a good portion of the earth, and Tom suspects the Brungarian rebels who obviously would like to capture Exman and use the space visitor to further their own evil purposes.

    With the security of Enterprises and Exman at stake, Tom creates two of his greatest inventions -- a Quakelizor to counteract the simulated earth tremors, and a container or "body" to house the energy from outer space.

    If the earthquakes cannot be stopped, the entire world will be threatened by destruction, and the Brungarian forces will conquer the earth. How Tom utilizes all his scientific knowledge to produce swift-action results and outwit the Brungarians makes one of the most exciting Tom Swift adventures to date.

    Baum, L. Frank - Wizard of Oz

    The Wonderful Wizard of Oz

    The Wonderful Wizard of Oz

    The Wonderful Wizard of Oz is a classic 1900 children's fantasy novel by L. Frank Baum about a young Kansas farm girl named Dorothy Gale who is swept away by a cyclone to a magical land.

    The Main Story

    The Arrival: Dorothy and her dog, Toto, get carried by a tornado into the Land of Oz. Their house lands on and kills the Wicked Witch of the East.

    The Journey:

    The Good Witch of the North gives Dorothy the dead witch's magical silver shoes (which were changed to ruby red in the 1939 film) and tells her to travel down the Yellow Brick Road to the Emerald City to ask the powerful Wizard of Oz to send her back to Kansas.

    The Companions:

    Along the way, Dorothy makes three friends who also want to ask the Wizard for a gift:
  • A Scarecrow who wants a brain.
  • A Tin Woodman who wants a heart.
  • A Cowardly Lion who wants courage.

    The Task:

    When they finally reach the Emerald City, the Wizard agrees to help them only if they first destroy the Wicked Witch of the West. After surviving traps and being captured by winged monkeys, Dorothy defeats the witch by throwing a bucket of water on her.

    The Twist:

    They discover that the Wizard is an ordinary man from Nebraska who is a "humbug" with no real magical powers. Even so, the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Lion realize they already possessed the brains, heart, and courage they were seeking all along. The Return Home: Dorothy learns from Glinda the Good Witch that her silver shoes have the power to take her anywhere she wishes, and she returns safely to Kansas with Toto.

    Core Themes

  • Longing for Home: No matter how strange or wonderful a place is, the emotional comfort of family and home matters most.
  • Self-Reliance: Real intelligence, compassion, and bravery come from within rather than from an outside authority.
  • Appearance vs. Reality: Figures of power (like the Wizard) can be illusions, and true strength comes from cooperation and friendship.

    Bradley, Marion Zimmer - Science Fiction

    The Door Through Space

    The Door Through Space

    The Door Through Space on Wikipedia is a 1961 science fiction novel by American writer Marion Zimmer Bradley.

    Story and Setting

  • • Planet Wolf: The novel takes place on Wolf, a desert world under a dim, heatless red-amber sun called F Coronis.
  • • Race Cargill: The protagonist is Race Cargill, a former top Terran Intelligence agent who has spent six years stuck behind a desk after a personal blood feud.
  • • The Conflict: Cargill is pulled back into active service to navigate deadly political intrigue, rescue his niece, and deal with an old enemy.
  • • Cultures and Themes: The story explores planetary colonization, the Terran Empire's trade network, and alien societies in the northern Dry Towns, including furred non-human natives ("Chocks" or the Chaka) and local customs where women wear stylized arm fetters.

    Coleridge, Samuel Taylor - Rime of the Ancient Mariner

    The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

    The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

    "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner" is a famous 1798 narrative poem by English poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge, written in the ballad form and published in Lyrical Ballads.
  • • The Interruption: An elderly, glittering-eyed Mariner stops a young man on his way to a wedding ceremony to force him to listen to a strange story.
  • • The Crime: The Mariner's ship sails south toward the Antarctic. When an albatross appears, the crew greets it as a good omen, but the Mariner impulsively shoots it with a crossbow.
  • • The Curse: The ship becomes trapped in a dead calm ("Water, water, everywhere, / Nor any drop to drink"). To punish him, the crew hangs the dead albatross around the Mariner's neck.
  • • Death and Reanimation: A ghost ship arrives carrying Death and Life-in-Death, who gamble for the crew. All two hundred sailors drop dead, leaving the Mariner alone with his guilt and hallucinations.
  • • Redemption: The curse lifts when the Mariner looks down at slimy sea serpents/snakes, suddenly appreciates their beauty, and blesses them. The albatross falls from his neck.
  • • Resolution: An angelic crew reanimates the ship to sail home before it sinks in a whirlpool. Rescued by a hermit, the Mariner is cursed to wander and periodically retell his tale as a moral warning.

    Key Themes

  • • Sin and Penance: The senseless killing of a creature brings divine or supernatural retribution.
  • • Sanctity of Nature: All living things are interconnected under God, and hubris leads to suffering.
  • • Romanticism: Emphasizes the supernatural, intense emotion, and the sublime power of the natural world.
    • AuthorSamuel Taylor Coleridge

    1 - The Hardy Boys and The Tower Treasure

    The first of an enduring series.

    The Hardy Boys will soon celebrate their 100th anniversary, but they remain the quintessential mystery and detective stories for younger readers. This first one, 'The Tower Mystery,' introduced the action, mystery, and suspense themes. The boys continue to deliver thrills to this day.

    It all starts with the boys, Frank and Joe, on their motorcycles delivering important papers to a lawyer in Willowville for their father, Fenton Hardy. He's the well-known private investigator who lives with his family in Bayport. A reckless driver almost forces them over the embankment. It is not long before they find that their friend Chet's yellow jalopy has been stolen, possibly by the same red-haired driver! Stolen loot may be the issue. Later a dying criminal confesses that the loot has been stashed "in the tower" and the Hardy Boys make an astonishing discovery.

    Dunsany, Lord - Book of Wonder

    Book of Wonder

    Book of Wonder

    The Book of Wonder - Wikipedia by Irish fantasy author Lord Dunsany is a landmark collection of fourteen short fantasy tales originally published in November 1912.

    Overview & Unique Origin

  • • Reversed Creative Process: Unlike most illustrated books, artist Sidney H. Sime drew the illustrations first, and Lord Dunsany wrote the stories afterward to explain and add mystery to the artwork (except for the final two tales).
  • • Tone & Style: Written in a lyrical, poetic, and ironic prose style, the stories blend fairy-tale wonder with dark humor, melancholy, and a sharp edge.
  • • Setting: Transports readers to otherworldly realms, ancient temples, dream-born kingdoms, and the "edge of the world" populated by jewel thieves, dragons, capricious deities, and strange entities like gnoles and the Gibbelins.

    Notable Stories

  • • "The Hoard of the Gibbelins": A knight tracks down a hidden treasure in a trap-filled tower by riding a dragon.
  • • "Chu-Bu and Sheemish": Two rival idols in an ancient temple compete for the devotion of their worshippers.
  • • "The Wonderful Window": A magical window that lets an ordinary man peer into a vibrant, fantastical world.

    Literary Legacy

  • • Served as a major formative influence on 20th-century fantasy masters including J.R.R. Tolkien, H.P. Lovecraft, and Ursula K. Le Guin.

    Wet Magic

    When four siblings journey to the seashore for a holiday, one of them unwittingly summons the sister of a mermaid who is captured by a circus, and the children set out to save the imprisoned being. After a daring midnight rescue, the children's reward is an incredible journey beneath the waves and into the hidden kingdom of the mermaids. But they soon find themselves in a race against time as they struggle to prevent a war and save their new underwater companions!     From the Earth to the Moon

    Jules Verne's science fiction duology—From the Earth to the Moon (1865) and its sequel Around the Moon (1870)—tells the story of an audacious post-Civil War plan to fire a manned projectile to the Moon using a giant cannon.

    From the Earth to the Moon (1865)

  • • The Premise: Following the American Civil War, the idle weapons experts of the Baltimore Gun Club—led by President Impey Barbicane—look for a new purpose and resolve to build a massive cast-iron space gun named the Columbiad.
  • • The Engineering: The club raises funds internationally, picks a launch site in Stone's Hill, Florida (eerily foreshadowing modern Florida space programs), and designs a hollow aluminum "space-bullet" capsule.
  • • The Crew: Barbicane's bitter armor-making rival, Captain Nicholl, and an eccentric French poet and adventurer named Michel Ardan join the mission, convincing the team to reshape the projectile into a passenger-friendly vehicle.
  • • The Climax: The Columbiad fires the capsule into the sky toward the Moon.

    Round the Moon

    Jules Verne's science fiction duology—From the Earth to the Moon (1865) and its sequel Around the Moon (1870)—tells the story of an audacious post-Civil War plan to fire a manned projectile to the Moon using a giant cannon.

    Around the Moon (1870)

  • • The Journey: The sequel picks up inside the flying projectile with Barbicane, Nicholl, and Ardan as they experience weightlessness, analyze space science, and gaze upon the Earth and the lunar surface.
  • • The Deviation: A near-collision with a passing asteroid alters their trajectory. Instead of landing on the Moon, the gravitational pull slings them into a permanent orbit around it.
  • • The Return: Using gases from explosive rockets to alter their course, they break free from lunar orbit and plunge back down to Earth, surviving a dramatic ocean splashdown.
